incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as last consolidated), particularly Articles 288 (incorporators), 289-290 (articles of incorporation), 291-296 (share subscription), 298-299 (payment and contribution inspection), 300 (incorporator report), 305 (organizational meeting), 312 (director and auditor appointment), 317 (registration of incorporation), 318 (effect of non-registration), 352 and 356 (share register and share certificates), 383 (director term), 393 (board of directors), 395 (representative director), 396 (board minutes) and 557 (registered office relocation); together with the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 168(1) and Value-Added Tax Act Article 8 for post-incorporation business registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Section of the District Court Registration Office (Court Registry) having territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered office, administered by the Supreme Court of Korea; e-filings are accepted through the I-Company electronic registration portal (www.i-company.go.kr) and Government24.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation Registration Application (Company Registration Application form) under Article 317 of the Commercial Act; after approval the registry issues the certified Extract of Corporate Registration (deung-gi sa-hang jeon-bu) and a corporate seal certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital exists under the Korean Commercial Act; the stated capital may be set at KRW 0 or any positive amount in the Articles of Incorporation. The incorporators must, however, pay in full the amount subscribed by each shareholder before registration and obtain a bank balance certificate from a domestic or foreign exchange bank confirming that amount. No separate statutory blocked escrow account is required for cash subscriptions; the bank balance certificate serves as the proof of paid-in capital. If any contribution is made in kind, a court-appointed examiner's report is required under Article 299 unless the in-kind contribution falls within a statutory exception. Foreign-currency subscriptions must comply with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and any applicable foreign investment reporting.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea - HomeTax electronic portal (hometax.go.kr); export declarations are processed by the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Determine whether the foreign entity has a Korean permanent establishment or only a taxable digital/electronic-services presence: a non-resident with a domestic business establishment must obtain a Business Registration Number from the competent district tax office; a non-resident without a domestic establishment that supplies electronic services to Korean consumers must use the non-resident simplified VAT registration on HomeTax. 2. File the Application for Business Registration under Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act with the district tax office (via HomeTax or in person) within 20 days of commencing taxable business, attaching the foreign entity's certificate of incorporation, foreign business registration/certificate of good standing, board resolution authorising the Korean presence, lease or service address evidence, certified Korean translation of foreign documents, and, if no permanent establishment is created, a written appointment of a Korean tax representative. 3. The district tax office reviews the filing and issues the 10-digit Business Registration Certificate/Number, which is simultaneously the Corporate Tax TIN, VAT ID and withholding tax account number for the Korean business. 4. A pure non-resident e-commerce supplier without a permanent establishment is not required to register for corporate tax, but must complete simplified non-resident VAT registration before supplies begin, and NTS will assign a non-resident VAT ID. 5. Immediately after receiving the Business Registration Number, the operator must register in the NTS electronic tax invoice system on HomeTax, because all VAT invoices issued by a registered corporation must be electronic.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - A Chusik Hoesa is a domestic corporation subject to the Corporate Tax Act and taxed on worldwide income as a separate taxable entity; shareholders do not include entity income as pass-through, and losses are not allocated to shareholders. Foreign corporations without a Korean permanent establishment are taxable only on Korean-source income, and no pass-through classification is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean law does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election or pass-through election for a Chusik Hoesa. The only relevant structural election is Korean consolidated group taxation for wholly-owned domestic subsidiaries electing to file a single corporate tax return under the Corporate Tax Act. Anti-hybrid rules under the Korean Adjustment of International Taxes Act operate automatically; there is no elective hybrid mismatch regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 - no general turnover threshold. Every person or entity that begins taxable business operations in Korea must apply for VAT registration within 20 days of commencement. Non-resident suppliers of electronic services to Korean consumers are also required to register under the simplified non-resident VAT registration on HomeTax, without any small-supplier threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Registered businesses must issue an electronic tax invoice for taxable B2B supplies through HomeTax or an NTS-certified electronic tax invoice service provider, and the e-invoice data must be transmitted to the NTS electronic tax invoice repository. HomeTax provides web filing and API/machine-to-machine EDI interfaces for integrated e-invoice transmission. Korea does not require per-transaction real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory digital stamping, or a cryptographic tax code; anti-fraud controls are enforced through mandatory electronic tax invoice issuance, central repository matching, invoice-number sequencing, and penalty taxes. Non-resident simplified VAT registrants serving B2C customers are generally not obliged to issue a domestic VAT invoice, but they must keep detailed electronic transaction records and file VAT returns through HomeTax.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act, a taxable supply of goods qualifies for the 0% rate if the goods are physically exported from Korea and the export is evidenced by a Customs Export Declaration. Services, including remote desktop access, remote screen sharing and unattended machine/IoT telemetry software, qualify for zero rating when supplied to a non-resident and the service is actually used or consumed outside Korea, with payment received in foreign currency. The supplier must prove foreign use through subscriber/customer location data, IP and geo data, usage logs, contracts, payment settlement records and foreign exchange receipts showing repatriation to Korea. Customs export declarations are not required for service exports, but the same evidential and foreign-exchange substantiation standards apply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration prepared in UNI-PASS and confirmed by Korea Customs Service as the definitive export clearance record
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (transport document) evidencing physical removal of goods from Korea and delivery to the foreign buyer
Commercial invoice, packing list, purchase order and export contract matching the Customs Export Declaration

Foreign exchange transaction certificate / foreign exchange earning certificate issued by a Korean authorized foreign exchange bank proving that export proceeds were received and repatriated in foreign currency (the Korean statutory substantiation equivalent of an FIRC)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the NTS or Korea Customs Service cannot verify the export or foreign-use documentation, or if the foreign exchange proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory deadline, the zero rating is reversed and the supply is recharacterised as taxable domestic supply. VAT at 10% is then assessed on the supply, plus penalty tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes - generally 20% of the understated tax, increased to up to 40% for fraudulent or wilful evasion - together with late-payment interest. Any previously refunded zero-rated VAT is clawed back with statutory interest, and if forged export documentation or false foreign-exchange evidence is identified, criminal penalties may be imposed under the Punishment of Tax Evaders, Etc. Act, including imprisonment and fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central bank and foreign exchange information system operator, acting jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the foreign exchange policy authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalised but notification-based foreign exchange regime. The Korean won (KRW) is freely convertible for most current-account transactions, including trade settlement, software royalties, and dividend remittances, subject to reporting to a licensed foreign exchange bank and the Bank of Korea's Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). Capital-account transactions, including foreign direct investment, inbound equity subscription, and cross-border loans, are permitted after a statutory report or permission under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. There is no mandatory surrender of export proceeds, and the won floats in an onshore market; offshore access to KRW is restricted, and settlement of offshore contracts may be constrained. In practice, profit remittances such as dividends require proof of retained earnings, foreign investment registration, and completed Korean withholding tax payments; banks will refuse payment if the FEIS report package is incomplete or if the economic substance of the software and IoT licensing revenue is not documented. The regime is therefore open and business-friendly but imposes strict bank-level paper trails, with no legal prohibition against retaining foreign currency in an approved foreign currency account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds for software, remote screen share, and IoT telemetry services must be collected within 6 months from the export or service provision date unless a licensed foreign exchange bank approves an extension. There is no statutory mandatory conversion ratio into KRW, and no forced surrender requirement; the exporter may retain the foreign currency in a Foreign Currency Settlement Account at a licensed Korean bank or convert it freely. Each collection must be recorded with the foreign exchange bank and filed into the BOK FEIS trade settlement record. If collection exceeds the statutory timeline, the exporter must file a delayed-collection or collection-cancellation report supported by the underlying service contract, delivery logs, and evidence of commercial non-performance or force majeure.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a primary corporate treasury account. Korean banking law does not recognise a foreign electronic money institution (EMI) wallet as a regulated deposit account for corporate cash management. A foreign EMI without a Korean branch license or a partnership with a Korean licensed bank cannot provide local KRW accounts, clearing rails, or FEIS reporting capability. Stripe and Paddle should be treated only as online payment aggregators for inbound card subscriptions and SaaS revenue, with settlement routed onward to a licensed Tier-1 Korean bank account. The Korean entity must maintain its real operating and foreign currency settlement accounts at a domestic foreign exchange bank, because capital contributions, trade reporting, dividend remittances, and statutory tax remittances require an onshore banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Tier-1 Korean banks generally require physical in-branch presence for opening corporate accounts, particularly for a newly incorporated Chusik Hoesa with foreign shareholders. Non-face-to-face digital on-boarding is commonly available to Korean-resident directors with a Korean Alien Registration Card, but for non-resident statutory directors the default standard is an in-person interview at the Korean branch or at a Korean bank's overseas office. Remote consular proxy opening is not standard practice and is generally rejected unless the bank agrees on a case-by-case basis to accept a notarised and apostilled power of attorney plus a physical appearance by a Korean attorney-in-fact. The bank will always conduct individually mandated KYC interviews with the UBOs and may require the original corporate seal, board resolution, and certified director identification before activating foreign currency or cross-border clearing functionality.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex foreign ownership chain with multiple passive investment vehicles and unclear ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) economic profile, causing heightened FATF Recommendation 24 scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of incorporation documents, memorandum and articles of association, full ownership tree, share registers, UBO declarations, six-month bank statements for each shareholder, source-of-wealth letters or certified CPA letters, apostilled passport copies, board resolutions approving the Korean entity formation, and signed commercial contracts showing the software and IoT business rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value digital licensing revenue flowing through third-party payment processors such as Stripe and Paddle, creating false-invoicing and disguised-cross-border-income suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-user software license agreements, SDK and API license contracts, order forms, technical support tickets, anonymised telemetry logs proving service delivery, cloud infrastructure invoices, internal payroll and office lease evidence, monthly Stripe and Paddle settlement reports, a transaction-by-transaction reconciliation ledger, and a SAR-ready narrative linking each remittance to a named client.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the 6-month export proceeds collection deadline and actual foreign currency receipts, causing the bank to suspect delayed or unreported export earnings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed statements of work, purchase orders, acceptance certificates, server utilisation reports, remote access session logs, export invoices, bank certificates of foreign currency deposit, FEIS transaction reports, and an approved extension letter from the foreign exchange bank if collection is delayed due to commercial disputes or force majeure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payer behaviour in which payments arrive from unrelated entities or personal accounts of Korean residents instead of the named foreign customer, creating nominee arrangement red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed payment direction letters from the actual end client, sub-contracting agreements, group intercompany service documentation, KYC/AML form for the third-party payer, board resolutions approving the transaction, UBO relationship disclosure, and a Korean legal opinion confirming that the payment structure complies with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign investor must file a Foreign Investment Promotion Act report through MOTIE or a delegated Tier-1 foreign exchange bank before making the inward remittance. The investor wires the share subscription consideration by SWIFT MT103 to the Korean entity's capital escrow account or foreign currency settlement account at the named Korean bank, with remittance instructions clearly stating foreign direct investment and share subscription purpose. The bank issues a certificate of foreign currency receipt, enters the transaction into the BOK FEIS under the appropriate capital transaction purpose code, and converts the funds to KRW through the licensed foreign exchange market. A Korean statutory auditor or certified public accountant then verifies paid-in capital and the actual issuance of shares; the entity completes registration of the capital increase with the Korean commercial registry and notifies the tax office. Stripe and Paddle receivables are not capital injections and must be processed as service export trade revenue, not as paid-in capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outward trade settlements for software procurement, cloud infrastructure, hardware for IoT devices, third-party professional services, and dividend remittances should be made using SWIFT MT103 through the licensed Korean bank, with the bank filing the required FEIS transaction report. For physical IoT hardware purchases with higher counterparty risk, the Korean treasury may use an irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit issued by the Korean bank and advised through the seller's bank, or documentary collections when working capital efficiency is preferred. All disbursements must be supported by original contracts, electronic tax invoices under the Korean VAT Act, and evidence of withholding tax payment where Korean-source royalties or dividends are remitted. Payment gateway payouts from Stripe or Paddle should be accumulated in the Korean entity's won account, then disbursed through the same FEIS-monitored SWIFT rails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable Korean won forward contracts with licensed foreign exchange banks, limited to documented underlying trade, service revenue, or cross-border cash flow exposure.

Cross-currency swaps and FX swaps for long-term foreign-currency capital flows or substantial multi-year IoT and software licensing contracts, subject to bank credit approval and FEIS transaction reporting.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only when hedging offshore KRW exposure with a clearly documented underlying commercial exposure; speculative NDF positions are prohibited without an underlying trade basis under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

Foreign currency option strategies and range forwards are permissible only as risk-reducing hedges on actual forecasted receipts or payables, with board-approved treasury policy and bank-compliant product suitability documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary general meeting of shareholders and approval of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate organ of Chusik Hoesa; no filing to a government agency, but meeting minutes form part of the corporate books
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of each business year; for a 31 December year-end the meeting must be held no later than 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the meeting within the statutory window exposes responsible directors to administrative fines of up to KRW 5 million under the Commercial Act and may make contested board resolutions unenforceable; if the company is subject to external audit, the audited financial statements cannot be made effective absent AGM approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and self-assessment payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months from the end of the tax-exposed business year; for a 31 December year-end, by 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inadequate filing triggers the statutory additional tax of 20% of the under-reported tax (increasing to 60% for concealment or fraud) and an overdue-late-payment surcharge of approximately 3.2% per month; persistent non-filing may result in forced NTS assessment, asset seizure, and formal designation as a delinquent taxpayer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax (local income surtax on the national corporate tax) return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government (Si/Gun/Gu) via the WeTax local tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same due date as the national corporate income tax return: within 3 months after the close of the business year (31 March following a calendar year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts a local tax delinquency surcharge equal to 3% within the first month plus 0.03% per day thereafter; continued default leads to tax seizure, public sale of assets, and cancellation of overdue tax benefits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value added tax preliminary and final periodic returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a consistent calendar-year operation: preliminary VAT return for the January-March period due 25 April; final VAT return for January-June due 25 July; preliminary VAT return for July-September due 25 October; final VAT return for July-December due 25 January of the succeeding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or under-filing triggers a late-file surcharge of 10% of the net VAT payable, plus the general 20%/60% underreporting penalties and a 0.03%-per-day overdue charge; VAT invoice violations carry separate penalties per invoice and can attract criminal sanctions in cases of systematic evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External auditor appointment, audit report delivery to the AGM, and submission of audited financial statements to the supervisory body
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART disclosure system; court registry in the commercial register if registration of approved financials is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: External auditor must be engaged within 4 months from the start of the business year (by 30 April for a calendar year); audit report must be presented at the AGM within 3 months after year-end; audited financial statements must be filed with FSS via DART within 14 days after AGM approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the company fails to appoint an auditor, the FSS designates one and the cost is borne by the company; failure to submit audited financial statements to the FSS is punishable by administrative fines and may trigger criminal liability of directors, loss of the statutory financial statements approval defense, and forced inspection by the FSS.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 21% national Corporate Income Tax on taxable income exceeding KRW 20 billion; plus 10% local income tax surcharge on national CIT, giving an aggregate headline burden of 23.1%; lower bracket rates are 9% up to KRW 200 million and 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: South Korea has no general patent box; reduced 9%/19% CIT rates apply to small and medium enterprises; Tax Incentive Limitation Law permits tax holidays or 30% to 100% corporate tax reductions for foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones and other prescribed zones; R&D expenditures eligible for tax credits up to 30% of qualifying cost for certain SME categories; no offshore shell company exemption exists and any incentive requires full economic substance and Korean-source bookkeeping

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Standard Return on Tax Base and Tax Amount (National Tax Declaration Form 14-5 series for Chusik Hoesa), filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; two preliminary corporate income tax instalments are paid during the year and are credited against the annual return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final annual corporate tax return and payment must be filed within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end the statutory deadline is March 31 of the following calendar year; foreign corporations may request limited extension under specific statutory conditions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of book income under K-IFRS or generally accepted accounting principles with taxable income; statement of financial position and profit or loss are attached, including adjustments for deferred tax, provisions, and foreign exchange gains or losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation must report only income attributable to its Korean permanent establishment; cloud software subscription or remote support fees are taxed only if a Korean PE exists, a dependent agency is present, or the income is properly attributable to a Korean fixed base; attach separate PE profit allocation statement using the OECD authorised OECD approach and avoid booking all global licensing revenue in Korea

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax deficits carried forward and deducted from current-year taxable income; statutory records of loss history, book closure, and tax audit adjustments are required
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses incurred by the Korean Chusik Hoesa or Korean PE may be carried forward; head-office losses of the foreign parent cannot be set off; loss carryforward period is 10 fiscal years; the return must identify the use of carried-forward losses and cannot use such losses against income that has not been properly reported to the NTS

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Tax Rate Application and Surcharge
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of national Corporate Income Tax at the progressive bracket rates and calculation of the 10% local income tax surcharge; interim instalment tax is credited; final tax payable and foreign tax credits are computed
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation with a Korean branch must apply the same progressive rates and local surcharge; no reduction is available merely because the foreign shareholder or parent is resident in a treaty country; any expected final withholding tax on profit remittances is not deductible in this line

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: R&D credits, foreign tax credits, employment promotion credits, special foreign investment tax reductions, and withholding tax credit for received interest or dividend income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident claiming treaty-based exemption or reduction on Korean-source income must complete the non-resident treaty application schedule and provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership declaration; digital service and IoT-related income cannot be recast as royalty income merely by calling it subscription if the true cross-border arrangement is for technical services or software licensing

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Non-Resident and Foreign Corporation Schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal shareholder information, foreign corporation net worth and accumulated earnings schedules, controlled foreign corporation disclosures, and distribution/dividend records for non-resident shareholders
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean company controlled by foreign shareholders, disclose all amounts remitted abroad as dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees; confirm whether the Korean filing entity is a CFC of a foreign parent, whether the ultimate owner is subject to Korean CFC rules, and whether any profit repatriation is eligible for DTA relief; failure to list the ultimate beneficial owner can trigger reassessment and penalties

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Non-Resident Tax Withholding and DTA Relief Return (National Tax Declaration Form 15-1 and related schedules) filed through HomeTax
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual withholding reconciliation combined with each remittance event
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Withholding taxes on any dividend, interest, royalty, or other outbound payment must be remitted to the NTS by the 10th day of the month following the payment date; annual treaty and withholding summary follows the corporate tax return cycle

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classification of remitted amount as dividend, royalty, interest, capital gain, technical service fee or business income; attached contract and Double Taxation Treaty analysis
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The payer must not reclassify economic dividends as interest or service fees to avoid withholding; NTS may recharacterise funding and licence agreements if the substance is equity; remote-screen-share IoT platform revenue may be treated as business profits, not royalties, unless the transferred right is a copyrighted work

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B - Beneficial Ownership and Residency Certificate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal status of the foreign recipient, recipient country, tax identification number, residency certificate validity, and declaration that the recipient is the beneficial owner
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty relief is denied unless the recipient is the beneficial owner and is subject to treaty-country tax on the income; interposed holding vehicles without economic substance will fail; NTS requires the Tax Residency Certificate to be issued by the foreign competent authority and, if needed, apostilled or certified

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C - Withholding Rate and Treaty Rate Applied
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of 22% combined domestic withholding (20% national plus 2% local income tax surcharge) and offsetting of applicable DTA-reduced rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The reduced treaty rate must be supported by the specific article of the bilateral treaty and must be applied net of domestic local income tax surcharge; if the treaty rate is lower than the domestic 22%, the payer must document the calculation and file the reduced withholding return, not wait for a refund

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under the Framework Act on National Taxes, non-filing or a false filing triggers additional tax of 20% of the unpaid tax for failure to file and 10% of the omitted tax for non-fraudulent underreporting; fraudulent underreporting triggers 40% of the omitted tax; unpaid withholding tax accrues statutory daily delinquency interest; criminal tax fraud under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act can result in imprisonment up to 10 years or fines up to five times the evaded tax; directors who caused or participated in the false declaration may be held jointly liable and placed on an NTS departure-restriction blacklist

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% combined for outbound cash or deemed dividends to non-resident persons, composed of 20% national Corporate Tax withholding plus 2% local income tax surcharge on the national withholding tax; DTA-reduced dividend rates of 10% or 15% commonly apply for qualifying corporate beneficial owners with certain shareholding thresholds
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief on Korean-source dividends, interest, or royalties, the non-resident recipient must file an Application for Tax Treaty Exemption/Reduction through the Korean payer with the NTS before or at the time of remittance; the applicant must submit a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the treaty jurisdiction competent authority in the calendar year of income receipt, a beneficial ownership statement confirming the receiving entity is not a pass-through or intermediary, evidence of shareholding period and voting control for dividend treaty rates, intercompany loan or licence contracts, and supporting financial records proving that the recipient has economic substance, staff, and real control of the intangible or debt claim; if the application is denied, the payer must withhold domestic 22% and the recipient may seek a corrective refund within applicable statutory periods
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding on cross-border royalties and intercompany interest is 22% combined (20% national plus 2% local income tax surcharge); many Korean DTAs reduce royalty withholding to 10% and interest withholding to 10% or, in some treaties, 5%; technical service fees and software subscription fees are often recharacterised by treaty rules as business profits taxable only through a Korean PE unless the transfer constitutes commercial income from copyrighted software

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5 billion in aggregate intercompany international transactions with foreign related parties triggers mandatory Local File preparation; a Master File is additionally required when the Korean entity is part of a group with annual consolidated revenue of at least KRW 100 billion and the Korean intercompany transaction volume reaches KRW 5 billion; simplified documentation may apply for lower materiality but NTS may request contemporaneous evidence on any audit
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea applies substance-over-form under Article 14 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and the beneficial ownership and economic substance requirement embedded in all applicable DTA articles; although Korea does not operate an offshore Economic Substance Regulations regime, the NTS may deny tax treaty benefits and recharacterise interposed Korean Chusik Hoesa structures when decision-making, risk control, employees, and Core Income-Generating Activities for the remote-screen-share or IoT telemetry business are located outside Korea; CFC rules attribute low-taxed offshore passive income to Korean controlling shareholders if the foreign company lacks real economic substance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent corporate income tax filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directors knowingly omit Korean-source subscription and telemetry revenue from the Corporate Income Tax Return, falsify K-IFRS books, create backdated invoices for software support, park revenue in undisclosed overseas accounts, and fail to pay corporate income tax and 10% local income tax surcharge
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3(1): imprisonment up to 10 years or a fine not exceeding five times the amount of evaded tax; Framework Act on National Taxes fraud additional tax of 40% of the omitted tax plus daily delinquency interest; NTS can impose 20% failure-to-file additional tax on unpaid amounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A court may pierce the Chusik Hoesa veil when directors used the corporation as a sham or conduit; directors are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt, face civil asset restitution and seizure of personal bank accounts, may be placed on the NTS departure-restriction blacklist (travel ban) pending tax payment, and can be sentenced to prison for concurrent criminal offences

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive shell company and treaty-shopping structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a Korean Chusik Hoesa with minimal capital, no employees, no office, no board meetings, and no operational control for the remote-screen-share and IoT software business while routing income and IP royalties through tax-haven subsidiaries solely to obtain Korean DTA reductions or deferrals under CFC rules
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: International Tax Adjustment Act Articles 4 and 5 permit NTS to recharacterise transactions according to economic substance and impose arm-length corrections; treaty relief is denied under DTA limitation-on-benefits or beneficial ownership clauses; Framework Act on National Taxes Article 14 allows disregard of sham entities; 40% fraud additional tax applies to any false treaty claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed false treaty declarations may be personally liable for the unpaid corporate tax and withholding tax of the shell company; NTS can blacklist beneficial owners and issue departure bans; directors face criminal prosecution for aiding tax evasion, with imprisonment terms applied under Punishment of Tax Evaders Act where the abuse is wilful

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, foreign exchange, and unlicenced payment-rail non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing outbound profit repatriation through unlicensed fintech intermediaries, crypto exchanges, or shell payment processors to avoid Korean withholding tax and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reporting; using structured remittances below the statutory threshold to hide dividend remittance or accepting proceeds from fraudulent remote-access subscription signups through Stripe/Paddle without customer due diligence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information imposes registration, customer due diligence, and suspicious transaction reporting obligations; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act Article 34 sanctions violations with imprisonment up to 3 years or fines up to KRW 100 million; unreported inbound or outbound transfers can be confiscated together with withholding tax and penalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally face criminal imprisonment and fines; funds routed through unlicensed rails are subject to disgorgement and civil asset forfeiture; Korean tax and financial authorities may issue a departure-control order (blacklisting) against directors and shareholders; the corporate veil is pierced for money-laundering and fraudulent conveyance when the company was used as an instrument of tax evasion
